A connection closes a mechanism, for exa: A connection closes a mechanism, for example between connecting rod and slider, without changing the reference bodies. It must allow the motion of the existing axes; a fixed connection can lock the mechanism.
A profile copies parameter values onto a: A profile copies parameter values onto a body while preserving its placement and reference bodies. Bodies remember their profile, but keep local values until you explicitly sync them. Sync replaces profile parameters, including local edits; use the sidebar for one body or queue all linked bodies here for OK. Built-ins are read-only, but you can inspect their values and duplicate one as your own starting point.
A servo holds a position, a motor holds: A servo holds a position, a motor holds a speed. Force limit, load and contacts decide what the body actually reaches.
Acceleration along the model's Z axis in: Acceleration along the model's Z axis in m/s². −9.81 is Earth's gravity, 0 makes all bodies weightless and positive values pull upwards. Stronger gravity means more load for actuators.
Actuated bodies must use their controls.
Adds an invisible, infinite floor at hei: Adds an invisible, infinite floor at height Z = 0 for bodies to land on. Switch it off when parts should move below Z = 0 or when the model has its own base.
An enabled override replaces the global: An enabled override replaces the global environment when this profile is applied. It can change the load on connected parts as well as the selected body; leave it off when the profile should follow the simulation's defaults.
Attachment body is missing or refers to: Attachment body is missing or refers to itself.
Both bodies must participate in the simu: Both bodies must participate in the simulation.
Cable is too stiff for this resolution. Reduce stiffness or use fewer segments.
Choose a clamped or pinned start before: Choose a clamped or pinned start before assigning a reference body.
Collision shapes are the simplified geom: Collision shapes are the simplified geometry Newton uses for contact: a box, a sphere or a convex hull around each body. They appear as coloured outlines over the model and reveal where contact geometry differs from what you see. This option decides whether the display is on when a window opens; the menu command “Show collision shapes” switches it in the current window. The display never changes how bodies collide.
Combine attraction with a sideways start: Combine attraction with a sideways starting velocity to create an orbit instead of a straight fall. Attraction grows near the centre; a larger softening radius keeps close passes from producing extreme forces. Initial velocity is applied only when starting a freely movable body.
Compound collision needs child groups or: Compound collision needs child groups or components.

Couple axes when one control should move: Couple axes when one control should move several parts, such as two gripper jaws. Limits on either side restrict the shared movement.
Coupled axes have no shared travel.
Coupled axis is missing or refers to its: Coupled axis is missing or refers to itself.
Coupling chains and cycles are not suppo: Coupling chains and cycles are not supported.
Defaults for every simulation. They take: Defaults for every simulation. They take effect the next time you press Start and apply to all bodies that do not use their own simulation settings.

Drag passive bodies. Use controls for ac: Drag passive bodies. Use controls for actuators.
Exclude contact between parts that are a: Exclude contact between parts that are already guided by a joint, such as a pin inside its bearing, when their overlap would otherwise jam the mechanism. The pair can then pass through each other, so the joint must provide the restraint. Contacts with other bodies remain active.
Fixed or actuated body. Use the controls: Fixed or actuated body. Use the controls.
Flexible bodies cannot also have a motio: Flexible bodies cannot also have a motion axis.
How exactly joints and contacts are solv: How exactly joints and contacts are solved. Quick suits setting up large mechanisms, Balanced everyday work, and Precise checking demanding contacts. Geometry and cable resolution stay the same, but motion can differ slightly between the levels.
Initial velocity needs a freely movable: Initial velocity needs a freely movable body.

Joint cycle detected. Closed chains are: Joint cycle detected. Closed chains are not supported.
Joint limits must include the initial po: Joint limits must include the initial position.

Like linear damping, but for rotation: s: Like linear damping, but for rotation: slows down spinning and wobbling bodies. 0 switches it off.
Locks the axis object in the model so th: Locks the axis object in the model so that no tool moves or rotates it by accident. It still follows its body.
Locks the connection object in the model: Locks the connection object in the model so that no tool moves or rotates it by accident. It still follows its body.

Slows down moving bodies, similar to air: Slows down moving bodies, similar to air resistance. At 1 /s a free body loses about two thirds of its speed per second; 0 switches damping off. More damping calms oscillations but also resists intended motion, so actuators need more force.

Sync queued for OK. Local values will be: Sync queued for OK. Local values will be overwritten.
The Python interpreter of the environmen: The Python interpreter of the environment that contains MuJoCo 3.3.7. Newton runs the simulation and the collision display in it as a separate process. Change this only when that environment has been moved or replaced; editing the model never requires it.

The collision shape decides where a body: The collision shape decides where a body can move. A box or hull closes openings and can block a mechanism; child components keep the gaps open.

The line becomes a bendable strand of fi: The line becomes a bendable strand of fixed length. A larger radius makes it stiffer and tighter in guides; stiff, finely segmented strands cost computation time.
The reference body must be visible and p: The reference body must be visible and participate in the simulation.

Use overrides when this body needs a dif: Use overrides when this body needs a different environment. It still collides with and pulls on connected neighbours, so local gravity can move an entire mechanism. Switch overrides off to inherit the global defaults again; a zero gravity vector instead explicitly makes this body weightless.
Use the flexible material end attachment: Use the flexible material end attachments for ropes and cables.
{bodies} follow this control. Their addi: {bodies} follow this control. Their additional load and limits also affect the leading axis; select a follower to change how far or in which direction it moves.
